comment_content:
In a DS project, your model can be a black box. Your data shouldn't be black
box. To understand what are the features, sizes, shape, their ranges, number
of unique values, how they are correlated to target variable etc. and a lot
more, you need EDA. And there are tons of ideas (hypothesis), you generate
while doing EDA. For example, in a regression problem, I realized doing
clustering and generating a new feature with clustered labels and then
proceeding with regression helped me increase accuracy. It made business sense
too.  I heard and saw many such benefits of EDA in many projects. And next,
EDA is advanced version of reporting or similar thing to visualization.
dashboard. Business wise, it adds or might add much more value than modelling.
If your model fails, your client may still be happy with insights you gave
from EDA. Hence, it's a selling point as well. May be backup deliverable. EDA
is exhaustive, there are some basic factors to check but it's not a single
point where you stop. If you are keen on getting good at EDA, go to kaggle,
pick most popular competitions and check out all kernels with EDA in title. If
you are keen on hands on, focus on coding as well. Hope this answers.
